title: Third-party access pathway exposure
description: The inability to control vendor remote access and privileged operations, enabling lateral entry.

title: Third-party compliance / legal exposure
description: The inability to maintain compliance due to third‑party non‑compliance, criminal acts, or other relevant legal actions.

title: Third-party concentration and systemic dependency
description: The inability to manage systemic dependency on a small number of critical ICT providers.

title: Third-party cybersecurity exposure
description: Loss of Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability and/or Safety (CIAS) from third‑party cybersecurity practices, vulnerabilities and/or incidents impacting products/services.

title: Third-party incident coordination failure
description: The inability to coordinate IR with vendors, cloud providers, and MSPs for containment and remediation.

title: Third-party incident response misalignment
description: The inability to integrate vendor IR processes and evidence sharing for coordinated containment.

title: Third-party physical security exposure
description: Loss of CIAS from physical security exposure of third‑party structures, facilities and/or physical assets impacting products/services.

title: Third-party supply chain relationships, visibility and controls
description: Loss of CIAS from downstream third‑party relationships, visibility, and controls impacting products/services.

title: Token theft and replay
description: The inability to protect and bind authentication tokens to devices/sessions, enabling replay and persistence.

title: Training data poisoning
description: The inability to prevent or detect malicious data injection that corrupts model behavior.

title: Unauthorized access
description: The inability to restrict access to only authorized individuals, groups, or services.

title: Unauthorized data access to sensitive data
description: The inability to enforce access controls for sensitive data at rest and in use.

title: Unauthorized device introduction
description: The inability to prevent rogue devices from connecting to corporate networks or OT environments.

title: Unauthorized physical access
description: The inability to restrict physical access to facilities, data centers, and critical rooms, enabling tampering and theft.

title: Unauthorized physical access to OT sites
description: The inability to protect substations, plants, and field cabinets from tampering and rogue connections.

title: Unauthorized PLC/RTU logic changes
description: The inability to detect and prevent unauthorized changes to controller logic and setpoints.

title: Unauthorized re-identification
description: The inability to prevent re-identification of de-identified data via linkage attacks or model inversion.

title: Uncontrolled exception management
description: The inability to manage risk exceptions with approvals, time bounds, compensating controls, and tracking.

title: Unmanaged BYOD and mobile risk
description: The inability to manage and secure mobile/BYOD devices, enabling data leakage and unauthorized access.

title: Unmanaged third-party and open-source vulnerabilities
description: The inability to track vulnerabilities in vendor products, OSS dependencies, and libraries.

title: Unmitigated vulnerabilities
description: Unmitigated technical vulnerabilities that lack compensating controls or other mitigation actions.

title: Unpatched internet-exposed services
description: The inability to remediate or restrict exposed services, increasing risk of remote exploitation.

title: Unsafe Autonomous Tool Execution
description: The inability to restrict AI agents from executing high-impact actions (e.g., database deletes, financial transfers) without human-in-the-loop authorization.12

title: Unsafe feature releases (privacy/AI)
description: The inability to gate releases with privacy and AI risk reviews, causing harmful or noncompliant features to ship.

title: Unsecured remote access
description: The inability to secure remote access paths (VPN, ZTNA), enabling credential theft and unauthorized entry.

title: Unsupported or end-of-life technology
description: The inability to retire or isolate EOL systems, increasing exposure to unpatched vulnerabilities.

title: USB/removable media exposure
description: The inability to control removable media, enabling malware introduction and data theft.

title: Use of product / service
description: The misuse of the product/service in a manner it was not designed for or approved for use.

title: Vehicle/rolling stock cybersecurity failures
description: The inability to secure connected vehicles and onboard systems, enabling remote manipulation or privacy breaches.

title: Visitor management failures
description: The inability to control visitor access and escorting, enabling social engineering and unauthorized access.

title: Vulnerability scanning misconfiguration
description: The inability to configure scanners and coverage properly, resulting in false negatives and blind spots.

title: Vulnerable and outdated components
description: The inability to manage third-party libraries and dependencies, enabling known exploits.

title: Weak authentication controls
description: The inability to enforce strong authentication (e.g., phishing-resistant MFA) for users, admins, and sensitive actions.

title: Weak configuration/change tracking
description: The inability to record and monitor configuration changes, creating unknown drift and control failures.

title: Weak database security
description: The inability to harden databases (auth, segmentation, patching), enabling injection, credential theft, or direct access.

title: Weak encryption at rest
description: The inability to encrypt sensitive data at rest using strong, approved algorithms and configurations.

title: Weak encryption in transit
description: The inability to enforce modern TLS configurations and prevent downgrade/weak cipher usage.

title: Weak penetration testing / validation
description: The inability to validate remediation effectiveness and exploitability through testing and verification.

title: Weak tokenization/anonymization controls
description: The inability to apply effective de-identification/cryptographic protection for regulated data, increasing privacy risk.

title: Weak vulnerability disclosure process
description: The inability to receive, triage, and remediate externally reported vulnerabilities responsibly.
